sentences.text: The genus Selenosteus belongs to the family Selenosteidae.
Selenosteus brevis possessed a wide skull featuring very large eye sockets.
Like other members of its family, this animal had weak jaw plates.
Its median dorsal plate was crescent-shaped and included a central keel.
The average length of its skull is about 16 centimetres.
The species Selenosteus brevis is known from the Famennian Cleveland Shale in Ohio.
Remains from the Frasnian Rhinestreet Shales of New York were attributed to Selenosteus in 1919, but this identification is considered doubtful.
A second species, S. kepleri, was described in 1901, but insufficient differences exist to justify its status as a separate species.
Fossils of Selenosteus have been found dating from the Frasnian to the Famennian periods.
Selenosteus lived during the Famennian stage, between 365.2 and 358.86 million years ago.
